title: Perfect complexes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E\in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], the derived category of all $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. A complex $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules on an open $U\subseteq X$ is *strictly perfect* if $\mathcal{E}^i=0$ for all but finitely many $i$ and each $\mathcal{E}^i$ is a direct summand of a finite free $\mathcal{O}_U$-module (Stacks, Cohomology of Sheaves, Definition [08C4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08C4)). $E$ is *perfect* if there is an open covering $X=\bigcup_i U_i$ such that for each $i$ the restriction $E|_{U_i}$ is isomorphic in $D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$ to a strictly perfect complex of $\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules (Stacks, Cohomology of Sheaves, Definition [08CM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08CM); the covering may be taken affine, and on $U_i=\mathrm{Spec}(A_i)$ a strictly perfect complex is the complex $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ of a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A_i$-modules, Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma [08EB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08EB)). The full subcategory of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ of perfect objects is denoted $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
